request:
I run a small provisions shop in Madina and I want to keep my price list on the computer instead of in my notebook. I want to add the things I sell with their prices. I want to see everything I sell, and look up the price of one thing. Sometimes I stop selling something, so I want to take it off the list.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: When a price goes up or down, do you want to change it on the list, and should the old price be kept so you can see what it used to be?
A: Yes, prices change all the time, especially sugar, rice and oil. I need to change the price of an item.
Q: Do some things come in different sizes or ways of selling (for example a single sachet and a full box), each with its own price?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: When you look up a price, will you type the full name exactly, or do you want to type part of a name (like "milk") and see everything that matches?
A: No preference: you decide.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
Every item now has a category, and you can view one category at a time. All 3 tests pass: the 2 existing ones, which I updated, and 1 new one for categories.

**What changed in `app.py`:**
- **Adding an item (`POST /items`)** now needs a `category` along with `name` and `price`, for example `{"name": "Milo", "price": 25, "category": "Drinks"}`. If the category is missing or blank, the item is refused.
- **Seeing one category (`GET /items?category=Drinks`)** lists only the items in that category. Capital letters don't matter, so "drinks" works too. Without `?category=`, `GET /items` still shows everything.
- **Every item shown** (in the full list, when you look one up, or after a price change) now includes its category.
- **Items already on your list:** I put them in a category called "Uncategorised" so nothing is lost when the app updates your saved list. You can't change an item's category yet, because you didn't ask for that. To move an old item into a real category, you would remove it and add it again.

Looking up a price, changing a price and taking an item off the list all work as before.

**Tests:** I added a category to the existing tests and added checks that adding an item without a category is refused. The new test checks that filtering by category returns only the right items, that capital letters don't matter, that an unknown category gives an empty list, that the full list still shows everything, and that an item keeps its category after a price change.
change: Every item has a category I choose, like Drinks, Toiletries or Foodstuff, and I want to see only one category at a time.
